post.contentHtml:
A Small Cap Working Behind Construction Sites: Shinwa (3447)

Shinwa (信和) is a metal products manufacturer listed on the Standard market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It makes and sells temporary construction materials (materials for structures used only while construction is under way, such as scaffolding) and logistics equipment used in factories and warehouses. It isn't a flashy sector, but its interim results make it worth asking whether it is a classic undervalued candidate: "earnings hold up, but the share price won't rise."

Where It Stands in Numbers

ItemDetails
Recent share price (value confirmed as of 2026-11-20)¥867
1-year share price changeAbout -7.4%
Expected dividend this year (annual)¥36 (¥18 interim + ¥18 year-end)
Expected dividend yield (based on ¥867, simple calculation)About 4.2%
Dividend for the previous fiscal year (FY ended March 2026)¥34

Dividend yield is the annual dividend divided by the share price. Dividing ¥36 by ¥867 gives a figure in the low 4% range. For reference, the share price was around ¥921 at the end of October, so it has fallen about 6% over the past few weeks. I could not confirm today's exact closing price through search, so I used the November 20 value as the basis.

What the November 11 Interim Results Tell Us

  • First-half (April–September) net profit was about ¥920 million, up about 5.3% year on year.
  • However, looking at July–September alone, it fell about 16%. The first-half total rose, but the quarterly trend slowed.
  • Progress toward the full-year net profit target of ¥1.6 billion is about 58%, lower than the five-year average (about 64%).
  • The company kept its full-year forecast unchanged: revenue of about ¥22 billion, operating profit of about ¥2.52 billion, and net profit of ¥1.6 billion.

Since net profit in the previous fiscal year was about ¥1.7 billion, this year's target assumes a slight decline. In other words, it is closer to a "company that defends its earnings level" than the kind of "growth story" the market tends to look for.

Interesting Point 1: The Dividend Is Rising, but the Share Price Fell

Although the dividend is set to increase from ¥34 to ¥36, the share price has fallen about 7% over the year. Raising the dividend while profits are shrinking pushes up the payout ratio (the share of net profit paid out as dividends), so whether the dividend can keep growing depends on future earnings. Dividend payments are scheduled to begin on December 1.

Interesting Point 2: Reliable Business Partners That Are Also Shareholders

Major shareholders include the steel trading company Hanwa and Alinco, each holding about 4.89%. Kazuya Kito, who appears to be linked to the founding family, holds about 1.8%, the US asset manager Dimensional Fund Advisors about 1.34%, and Daiwa Securities about 1.08%. Large institutions are not heavily invested, so trading volume is low, and Korea's National Pension Service holds no stake. With a median annual trading value of only about ¥32 million, low liquidity is something individual investors must keep in mind.

Things to Check

  • Sensitivity to the construction cycle: The core temporary materials business is affected by construction starts and by labor and material prices. My own estimate is that this third-quarter slowdown may reflect such conditions, but I could not confirm that the company has stated a specific cause.
  • Whether second-half profit targets are met: The remaining net profit target is about ¥680 million. The key is whether the second half can keep pace with the first.
  • Low trading liquidity: Bid-ask spreads may widen, and it may be hard to buy or sell at the price you want.

Summary

Shinwa is not a flashy growth stock but a small value stock with stable earnings and a dividend yield above 4%. On the other hand, its recent quarterly profit decline and low liquidity are clear weaknesses. The key is to watch whether the profit decline continues in the next quarterly results and whether the company can meet its full-year targets.
